Spatial Durbin model

The paper extends Chanda and Kabiraj (2020) through a reproducible workflow.

Mendez, Kabiraj & Li (2026)Abstract, p. 17303 / 12
The published abstract explicitly says three empirical fronts. They are interactive visualization of convergence patterns, assessment of spatial dependence in the main econometric specification, and a spatial Durbin model for spillovers. The cultural analysis is an exploratory closing extension, not a fourth empirical front in the abstract.

Mendez, Kabiraj & Li (2026)§3.2, p. 180; Figures 6–704 / 12
These are Global Moran’s I statistics using the six-nearest-neighbor spatial weights. Initial luminosity refers to 1996 per-capita luminosity. Growth covers 1996–2010. Spatial clustering motivates the econometric specification, but the statistics do not establish causal transmission across districts.

Mendez, Kabiraj & Li (2026)Table 4, p. 18608 / 12
Entries are effects of initial log luminosity in Model 4. Table 4 also gives standard errors and indirect effects. Indirect effects are negative in all seven specifications and significant in five. Do not claim that every indirect effect is significant. The baseline uses six nearest neighbors; the other six matrices test sensitivity. No re-estimation was performed for these slides.
REGION 2026 / INDIA

Interpretation remains associational

MODEL

Shared conditions

Geography, institutions, infrastructure and omitted variables can contribute to spatial dependence.

MEASUREMENT

A limited observation window

One growth interval and a luminosity proxy constrain what the estimates explain.

The analysis does not identify a causal effect of changing one district on another.

Mendez, Kabiraj & Li (2026)§3.3, pp. 184–188; §409 / 12
Preserve the paper’s reduced-form interpretation. Spatial links may reflect true interaction, common influences, omitted variables and light blooming across boundaries. Nighttime luminosity is a proxy affected by electrification and urbanization. A cross-sectional 1996–2010 growth regression does not identify annual convergence dynamics. The estimates should not be presented as causal benefits of a specific intervention.

An exploratory link to culture

+0.370

Media-based consumption

Spearman correlation · p = 0.037

−0.404

Community participation

Spearman correlation · p = 0.022

Across 32 states and union territories, luminosity relates differently to these two forms of cultural participation.

Mendez, Kabiraj & Li (2026)§4.3, pp. 188–189; Figure 910 / 12
This is a separate exploratory analysis at the state level, not the 520-district convergence sample. It uses NSS 47th Round cultural participation data (July–December 1991) and the Consistent and Corrected Nighttime Lights series for 1992. Spearman rank correlations are 0.370 (p=0.037) for cultural telecast and −0.404 (p=0.022) for socio-cultural participation. Four other cultural dimensions do not have statistically significant associations. Correlation does not establish a causal cultural effect.
